label: debug
note: Before the runner and this log existed, replication 0 of D01 and of P3 at STD was run once each by calling the pipeline directly on uncommitted code, to see that it ran end to end and to time it (about 57 s each). Their numbers were printed, not kept, and are superseded by the logged runs that follow. About 1,200 single-family SPA calls on i.i.d. noise were also made to check the test's size outside the pipeline. No held-out scenario was run.

label: pilot
note: Stopped by the session (SIGTERM) before its one replication finished: 106 minutes of wall time and 2 hours 31 minutes of CPU time, with the sampler at 200 warm-up and 200 kept draws per chain (a fifth of the default 1,000 and 1,000). No result was written. The start record above therefore has no end record.

label: development
note: Session 5M, outside the runner, on uncommitted code: replications 0 to 39 of D11's world, SPA only, a fixed 999 resamples per family, to choose the centre of the hedge-aware resamples. Six tests on the same resamples: the 3.0 test, the hedge re-estimated and centred at the live mean, at the resamples' own mean, at the window's least-squares intercept (adopted in PROTOCOL_v3.1 section 5.1), the in-window intercept as the statistic, and the 3.0 test on the true hedged returns. Numbers: results/manhattan_sim/v2/DEVELOPMENT_NOTES.md section 1. Not a pilot of record. No held-out scenario was run.

label: development
note: Session 5M, outside the runner, on uncommitted code: replications 0 to 11 of D11's world with the factor's annualised Sharpe ratio raised from 0.6 to 0.8 and the exposure's annual standard deviation from 0.3 to 0.4 (in memory only: no scenario was added), the same six tests at 999 resamples. Numbers: DEVELOPMENT_NOTES.md section 2. It is the top corner of the one-factor ranges SIM_PREREG_v2 gives held-out scenario H12; it is not H12, which is not coded.

label: development
note: Session 5M, outside the runner, on uncommitted code: replications 0 to 3 of each HB development scenario with the first version of the analytic model (families independent, no common shock). It showed shared luck read as a shared edge in D05 replication 1, which is why PROTOCOL_v3.1 section 7.1 has a common forward shock. Numbers: DEVELOPMENT_NOTES.md section 3. Also by hand: D02 replication 0 (three times) and D05 replication 1 (three times) with per-family printouts or timings, and runner smoke tests on programmes of a few batches written to a temporary directory.

label: development
note: Session 6M, outside the runner: the pilot's 12 replications of each of D02, D05, D08 and D10 at HB replayed with the pilot's own code (c22815235975c486, before any edit), keeping for every family and review its true Sharpe ratio, estimates, the six models' Pi, the forecast PP under each model and its tier. Each of the 48 replays equals its run record on the counts behind M8. Variants of the dormancy rule were then scored on the stored fits, one element changed at a time: cut-offs 0.02, 0.01 and exactly 0; reactivation at 0.05; 1, 2 and 3 forward years; three consecutive reviews; the forecast under the central model only; and a second condition Pi^max below 0.05, 0.10 or 0.20 with 0, 252 or 504 forward days. Numbers: results/manhattan_sim/v2/DORMANCY_DIAGNOSIS.md part 1. It is the evidence for change 5 of PROTOCOL_v3.1 (section 9.1). Not a pilot of record. No held-out scenario was run.

label: development
note: Session 6M, outside the runner, on the stored fits of note-6M-01: the forecast PP recomputed from the stored posterior draws with two other definitions of its event (each model judges its own future; the Promising tier instead of Statistically supported), with this session's random numbers, and the pilot's rule replayed on each. Numbers: DORMANCY_DIAGNOSIS.md section 1.3. Neither was adopted.

label: development
note: Session 6M, outside the runner, on the stored estimates of note-6M-01: for every family and review, three posteriors of an edge of at least 0.25 from the same reserve and forward estimates and standard errors: the central model's, a plain normal prior with the population's own mean and variance, and the population's true shape. Calibration error at year 10 in D08: 0.101, 0.102 and 0.009. Numbers: DORMANCY_DIAGNOSIS.md part 2. It is the evidence for the limitation stated in PROTOCOL_v3.1 section 7.2(d). The model was not changed.

label: development
note: Session 6M, outside the runner: 48 replications (12 of each of D02, D05, D08 and D10, the pilot's worlds) at HB with yearly reviews (MANHATTAN_SIM_EVAL_YEARS=1,...,10 in place of the pre-registered years 2, 4, 7 and 10), with the code of commit 9b1f068 and the revised dormancy rule; the first nine ran while the working tree held uncommitted edits to other files, and the experiment was stopped once and resumed. The dormancy rule of 3.0 and variants of the revised rule were replayed on the stored fits. Reported: premature elimination under both rules at this cadence, and the share of families with a true edge that reach Statistically supported by years 4, 6 and 10, by true Sharpe ratio. Numbers: DORMANCY_DIAGNOSIS.md parts 3 and 4. It changes a declared reduction of the pre-registered pipeline (SIM_PREREG section 2.5(c)), so it is a development experiment only: it decides nothing and is pooled with no run of record.
